response.passage: Rohan visited a local stationery shop to buy supplies for his project. He noticed that the price of a notebook is 20 rupees more than the price of a pen. He decided to represent this relationship as n = p + 20, where n is the cost of a notebook and p is the cost of a pen. The shopkeeper mentioned that a special set of two pens and three notebooks costs exactly 150 rupees. Rohan wrote the second equation as 2p + 3n = 150. To find the individual prices, he decided to use the substitution method. He replaced n in the second equation with (p + 20), resulting in 2p + 3(p + 20) = 150. Upon simplifying, he calculated 5p + 60 = 150, which led to 5p = 90, giving p = 18. He then found n = 38. Rohan checked his work by verifying that 18 and 38 satisfy both equations. He was pleased to find that the solution (18, 38) works perfectly for the pair. He also noted that the equation p = 18 is a valid linear equation in two variables, which can be written as 1p + 0n = 18, representing a vertical line on a graph.
response.summary: Rohan uses a system of linear equations to determine the individual costs of pens and notebooks. By substituting one variable into the other, he successfully solves for both prices and verifies his result.
